claims.claim: At the advertised knight-encounter staging configuration, the idealized ambiguous move has the two global possibilities ±r, and both stated branches are exclusive and end in K(q+r;a,r,f).
claims.evidence: The 48 signed coordinate symmetries were enumerated exactly. The stabilizer fixing −f and −a has two elements and sends r to exactly {r,−r}. Integer-coordinate simulation of both subsequent branches found only unit or idle moves, distinct destinations, no edge swap, and endpoint {q+r,q+r+a,q+3r+f}=K(q+r;a,r,f).
claims.witness: For the −r branch the post-ambiguity positions are (q+r,q+2r+f,q+r+f), followed by endpoint (q+r+a,q+3r+f,q+r). For the +r branch they are (q+r,q+2r+f,q+3r+f), then (q+r,q+r+f,q+3r+f), followed by (q+r+a,q+r,q+3r+f).
claims.search_method: Exhaustive enumeration of all signed coordinate permutations and direct exact-integer verification of every stated synchronous round.

claims.claim: From the advertised ordinary-transition staging configuration, the distinct-choice branch gives D(q;d,e,f), while the contact-and-rotation branch gives D(q;e,d,f), without a collision or edge swap.
claims.evidence: Both assignments (d,e)=(a,−r) and (−r,a) were checked. Moving q+f to q+e+f gives {q,q+d,q+e+f}=D(q;d,e,f). In the other branch, q+f first moves to q+d+f, after which q→q+e and q+d→q give {q,q+e,q+d+f}=D(q;e,d,f). All displacements are unit or idle, destinations remain distinct, and no pair traverses one edge in opposite directions.
claims.witness: The two rotation edges are {q,q+e} and {q,q+d}; because d and e are distinct orthogonal signed unit vectors, they are different edges rather than an edge swap. The stationary third position q+d+f is distinct from both destinations.
claims.search_method: Exact-integer enumeration of both choices of d and both advertised branches, with collision and directed-edge-swap assertions at every round.

claims.claim: From the advertised outer-reset conversion staging configuration, every choice of d, x and the ±d conversion branch is exclusive and ends in K(s;y,d,x).
claims.evidence: All eight combinations of d∈{a,−r}, x∈{e,−f}, and sign ± were enumerated. After conversion and the sign-dependent correction, both signs give the positional set {s,s+x,s+2d+x}. The final simultaneous moves s+x→s and s→s+y give {s,s+y,s+2d+x}=K(s;y,d,x). Every round has distinct destinations, only unit or idle moves, and no edge swap.
claims.witness: For +d, M moves from s+d+x to s+x while C remains at s+2d+x. For −d, C is at s+x while M moves from s+d+x to s+2d+x. Thus the same unlabeled set precedes the common final step in both branches.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive exact-integer checking of two d choices, two x choices, and two conversion signs, including every intermediate synchronous round.

claims.claim: The three retained positional macros do not define or prove a visibility-one algorithm with at most 76 shades.
claims.evidence: Under the source definition, an algorithm requires a shade set Cl, a nonempty initialization map Init for every eligible cave, and a total local-view transition function T, followed by proof for every permitted execution. The three macros supply none of these objects and establish neither orbit consistency, staging reachability, invariant composition, nor perpetual coverage.
claims.witness: The macros are explicitly limited to conditional, unlabeled positional transitions. Exact correctness of those coordinates cannot supply the missing shade transitions or a global PEP proof.
claims.search_method: Direct structural comparison of the three macro proofs with the source definitions of algorithm, execution, and PEP.

claims.claim: If a visibility-one algorithm for exactly three Batdroids without common chirality solves PEP, then on every N×N×N cave with even N≥14, every permitted execution has infinitely many rounds in which some Batdroid's current rule admits more than one global destination.
claims.evidence: Fix any permitted execution and suppose it has an ambiguity-free suffix. An even cube has eight centers, so one is empty at the suffix start. PEP forces a first later visit. Its entrant cannot have been lost: a non-idle move from a lost visibility-one view has all six unit directions in its symmetry orbit and is therefore ambiguous. Thus another Batdroid was adjacent immediately before entry. The source's four exhaustive adjacency cases then use only unambiguity on the realized suffix: the robots become confined to a central coordinate slice, a line plus an isolated stationary robot, or an all-idle configuration. Each contradicts PEP. Hence no ambiguity-free suffix exists.
claims.witness: The proof is suffix-local: reflection across a central slice forbids an unambiguous move out of that slice; a paired internal view permits unambiguous movement only along the pair's line; and a lost robot permits only idle. For N≥14, the source's distance bounds keep the relevant center-near robots away from walls throughout the case split.
claims.search_method: Independent quantifier check and reconstruction of the source center-case proof after replacing global well-definedness by the assumed unambiguous suffix of one arbitrary execution.

claims.claim: The recurrent-ambiguity obstruction is shade-blind and does not provide a lower bound separating 76 shades from 77.
claims.evidence: The recurrent-ambiguity proof depends only on positions, walls, visibility-one symmetries, and whether a movement direction is invariant. Coordinate transformations preserve all displayed shades, and the proof neither identifies shades nor uses the cardinality of Cl. Its conclusion is therefore compatible with algorithms having 76, 77, or any other positive number of shades.
claims.witness: The theorem requires ambiguity to recur, while the target expressly permits ambiguity. It excludes no shade count and consequently cannot establish that every at-most-76-shade algorithm fails.
claims.search_method: Dependency audit of every step in the recurrent-ambiguity argument against the source model's positional and shade components.

claims.claim: Neither alternative in the target is established.
claims.evidence: The draft supplies no at-most-76-shade tuple (Cl,Init,T) and no proof of PEP for such a tuple. It also supplies no universal impossibility result for algorithms with at most 76 shades. The shade-blind recurrent-ambiguity condition cannot fill either gap.
claims.witness: The positional macros lack colored local rules and global coverage, while the only obstruction permits every positive shade count. Thus neither the construction alternative nor the 77-optimality alternative follows.
claims.search_method: Compared the exact two-way source target with every claimed result and its proved scope.

target_evidence: The recurrent-ambiguity theorem is a correct, nontrivial necessary condition on every execution of any prospective solution, and the three finite positional calculations are correct within their expressly limited scope. This is valid partial progress, but it neither constructs an ambiguous visibility-one PEP algorithm using at most 76 shades nor proves that all such algorithms are impossible. The draft's PARTIAL resolution label accurately reflects that gap.
